cells.tense: You're here, with the pen, and something is ending on time.
cells.place: where one thing has to end for good before the next can start
cells.ask: Tend one thing that's starting to come up in the cleared space — water it, check on it, keep your hands off the outcome — and you'll have room to let go the moment something is finished, with no fight in it.
cells.core: You're here, with the pen, and something is ending on time. You're not being torn from it and you're not quitting it early — it's finished, and your hands are opening because there's nothing left to hold. What people call loss, you're finding is mostly room. There's space now that wasn't there, and you're standing in it rather than mourning what used to fill it.
cells.sheetLine: It's done, and your hands opened on their own.

cells.tense: You're already living in the version where you've given it up.
cells.place: where one thing has to end for good before the next can start
cells.ask: Pick one thing you've been about to put down and stay with it a little every day until it actually finishes — plain repetition, nobody watching — and letting go will start to feel like completing something instead of leaving it.
cells.core: You're already living in the version where you've given it up. The ending hasn't arrived yet, but you've decided it's noble to get there first, so you're putting things down while they're still half-done and calling that release. It isn't clearing — it's leaving, and some of it is for an audience. What you let go of early doesn't make room; it just leaves things unfinished behind you.
cells.sheetLine: You're calling it letting go. It's leaving early.

cells.tense: The door is already closed and you're still holding the handle.
cells.place: where one thing has to end for good before the next can start
cells.ask: Choose one thing that is actually worth carrying and carry it properly — a real hold, around it rather than clenched on it — and notice what your hands quietly drop when they're busy holding something that deserves them; the finished things will leave on their own then, and it will feel like completion, not defeat.
cells.core: The door is already closed and you're still holding the handle. The thing has run its course and you know it, but your grip has outlasted the reason for it, and the holding has become the whole job. You're tired in a way rest doesn't fix, because what's wearing you out isn't the weight — it's keeping hold of something that's already over. The grip is doing the work your hands used to do.

cells.tense: Your hands are already open and you haven't looked down to see it — or they're closed and you'd swear they weren't.
cells.verb: letting go without knowing you have
cells.place: where one thing has to end for good before the next can start
cells.ask: Find one small thing that's already growing in the space you cleared and tend it for a week, plainly, and say out loud that you're the one who made the room for it — then letting go becomes something you do, not something that happens to you.
cells.core: Your hands are already open and you haven't looked down to see it — or they're closed and you'd swear they weren't. Something has ended in your life and you're describing it as still pending, or something is still gripped and you're describing it as done. Either way, the letting go is being run by someone, and you keep saying it isn't you. The release is real. The claim on it is missing.
cells.sheetLine: You've already let go, or you haven't. You're the last to know which.
